author: Thucydides
title: History of the Peloponnesian War
blurb: Power transitions, alliance management, the decay of norms under pressure, and what a leader is for. The oldest case study of competitive escalation on record — and still the sharpest.

author: Sun Tzŭ
title: The Art of War
blurb: Competition as a discipline of calculation, positioning and intelligence, in which the supreme achievement is to win without fighting. The shortest text in the corpus and the most quoted in boardrooms.

author: Kautilya
title: Arthashastra
blurb: The most systematic management handbook of the ancient world: the elements of organized power, the geometry of rivals and allies, and a sixfold playbook of strategic postures.

author: Niccolò Machiavelli
title: The Prince
blurb: Early detection of slow-building trouble, the brutal politics of leading change, and how to act when luck governs half of everything. Read here as diagnostics, not as cynicism.

author: Hugo Grotius
title: Mare Liberum — The Freedom of the Seas
edition: Translated by Ralph Van Deman Magoffin (1916)
blurb: The founding argument for open trade routes and a rules-based commercial order, written as a legal brief for a joint-stock company. Where the idea of the open global market begins.

author: Francis Bacon
title: Essays — Of Empire · Of Innovations · Of the True Greatness of Kingdoms and Estates
blurb: Competitor monitoring as a standing function, innovation against the drag of custom, and why the valuation of a rival's real strength is the error-prone judgment call in strategy.

author: Thomas Mun
title: England's Treasure by Forraign Trade
blurb: The classic statement of trade-balance thinking by a director of the East India Company — the mercantilist worldview that still returns in every era of trade war, and a period portrait of the compleat international manager.

author: Thomas Hobbes
title: Leviathan
blurb: Why competition without enforceable rules destroys investment, why sovereign actors live in permanent mutual surveillance, and why agreements need enforcement mechanisms to mean anything.

author: Adam Smith
title: The Wealth of Nations, Book IV
blurb: The demolition of zero-sum trade thinking — and, less quoted, the concessions to security: 'defence is of much more importance than opulence.' The permanent argument between efficiency and resilience.

author: Carl von Clausewitz
title: On War
blurb: Strategy under uncertainty: friction, the fog of unreliable information, and the subordination of operations to policy. The deepest text ever written on why execution diverges from plan.

author: Alfred Thayer Mahan
title: The Influence of Sea Power upon History
blurb: Infrastructure as strategy: the sea as a 'wide common', trade routes as arteries, and six enduring conditions of positional power. The grammar of today's chokepoint and supply-chain debates.

author: Halford J. Mackinder
title: The Geographical Pivot of History
blurb: The closed world system: once every market and region is claimed, every shock 'will be sharply re-echoed from the far side of the globe.' The founding paper of modern geopolitics.
